events.title: The Regency of the Golden Court
events.external: zin_aenor.210 fires it when the Court takes the seals
events.desc: No king is named. The Regency rules in the crown's name, and the crown's name has never been better for trade.

events.title: The Temples Are Displeased
events.desc: The High Confessor preaches that a crown without a king offends the god, and the temples of Parim are full of people who agree with him.

options.text: The Regency answers to the Concord, not the temples.

events.title: Prince Eronel Asks for the Crown
events.desc: Prince Eronel of Arcedor asks the Regency to crown him. He has the rooms, the friends and the gold leaf, and lacks only the anointing.

events.title: A Regency Without End
events.to: the Aenor realm, while the Court still rules
events.desc: Three years on, the Regency still rules for a crown nobody wears. The feasts are as long as the late King's, and the toasts are shorter.

events.title: The Speaker of the Concord
events.external: zin_aenor.210 fires it when the Dominions take the seals
events.to: the Aenor realm and every Concord dominion
events.desc: The dominion lords elect a Speaker to hold the seals, and every charter is rewritten as a Free Charter. The Speaker's first act is to read the Charters of Parim aloud from the first word.

variants.text: The lords of the Concord have chosen a Speaker, and our charter is rewritten as a Free Charter. The seals of Parim now rest with the Concord and not with a crown.

options.text: The crown is first among equals.

events.title: The Temples Ask Their Place
events.desc: The High Confessor asks what the Concord wants of the god's temples. The Speaker has twenty-six charters on the table and not one of them mentions a pulpit.

options.text: Keep the temples as they are.
The temples answer to each dominion.

events.title: A Concord Council Every Year
events.desc: The Concord Council meets again, as it did in 4A 212, and the Speaker means to see that it meets every year after.

events.title: The People's King
events.external: zin_aenor.210 fires it when the Host takes the seals
events.desc: [zin_loc_eindil] is hailed, not crowned, by the captains and scholars of the realm. He asks for the Lost Cause and not for a throne.

events.title: The Temples Do Not Kneel
events.desc: The temples will not bless a king without a house. Their doors stand open to the people and shut to the stranger who would lead them.

options.text: Let them pray as they like.

events.title: King Eronel
events.external: zin_afrit.23 fires it two days after the heir is crowned
events.desc: Prince Eronel is crowned with the temples' blessing. The Chancellor stands at his right hand, and the crowd cheers a face it hardly knows.

events.title: A King Who Signs
events.desc: The new king signs everything the Chancellor brings him. The court calls it a gift for the work of the seals, and the Chancellor does not correct it.

events.title: The King Afraid
events.external: zin_aenor.250 fires it three days after the proof is laid before the King
events.desc: The Golden King has not slept since the proof was laid before him. He eats nothing his own tasters have not touched, and for the first time in twenty years he asks the Lost Cause for guards.

events.title: The Temples Close Their Doors
events.external: zin_aenor.260 fires it when the Faithful rise against the King
events.desc: Half the temples of Parim bar their doors to the King's men. The other half open them to the frightened.

options.text: The King is still the King.

events.title: The Golden King Rides Out
events.desc: In this telling of the age, the Golden King rides at the head of his league for the first time in his life. Behind him the gilt on the banners is new, and the men beneath them are not.

events.title: A King Who Lived
events.external: zin_aenor.261 fires it when the King endures
events.desc: The King lives. In this telling of the age, the Golden Court goes on, and so does its gold.

events.title: The God-King's City
events.to: the Aenor realm while the Deliverer rules it, and the Worshipdom
events.desc: Parim has never been cleaner or quieter. The granaries are full, the beggars are fed, and fewer people ask questions in the taverns.

variants.text: Parim is quiet because the Couriers' Chapter has made it so. The granaries are full, the taverns are listened to, and the Council reads the week's whispers every dawn.

events.title: The King Withdraws to Pray
events.external: zin_afrit.32 fires it when the Deliverer leaves Parim and rules Aenor
events.to: the Aenor realm and every Concord dominion
events.desc: King [zin_loc_deliverer] has withdrawn into retreat to pray for the realm. Chancellor Merovan holds the seals until he returns.

variants.text: Riders from Parim: King [zin_loc_deliverer] has withdrawn into retreat to pray for the realm, and Chancellor Merovan holds the seals until he returns. Our lord is asked to pray as well.

events.title: The King Returns Pale
events.external: zin_afrit.34 fires it when the Deliverer is back in Parim and the secret holds
events.desc: The King is back in Parim. He walks slowly and receives no one for a month. The temples say the god bears the realm's sorrows.

events.title: Talk of an Impostor
events.external: zin_afrit.40 (Denounce him) and the historical option of zin_eindil.82 fire it
events.desc: The chancery warns every dominion: a foreign impostor claims the blood of Aen and speaks against the King.

events.title: The Dominions and the Impostor
events.desc: Parim says the stranger is a liar. Our own captains, who have heard him, say he talks sense.

options.text: Let him speak in our halls.

events.title: What Is Owed to a False God?
events.external: zin_afrit_reveal fires it three days after the name is spoken, to every Aenor realm
events.desc: A name has been spoken in Parim, and the court is deciding what it owes.

variants.text: The court knows what its king is. Some lords leave Parim by night. Most stay, from faith or from fear.
The temples of Aenor stand accused. The Houses of the First Light served the false god, and those who work in them are asking whether they served a lie.

options.text: Let the lords who flee go.

events.title: The Captains' Regency
events.external: zin_aenor.300 fires it one day after the throne is abandoned, when the Captains' Regency takes the seals
events.desc: Lord-Commander Tarec and the frontier captains have taken the seals until a king returns. Nobody asks which king.

events.title: Empty Temples in Parim
events.desc: Half the priests have gone east with their god. The other half pray for forgiveness. The poor still come for bread.

options.text: Feed them from the crown's stores.
